coverage_notes: Read in full: all 42 files in the unit (agent_control_cli.ex all 3,408 lines; orchestrator.ex, build_gate.ex, agent_environment.ex, cli.ex, recent_merge.ex, executor_events.ex, env.ex, decision_attention.ex, workflow.ex, agent_event_feed.ex, executor_command_cli.ex, build_orders_cli.ex, units_cli.ex, github_usage_cli.ex, decision_answer.ex, decision.ex, decision_revision_dispatch.ex, decision_enrichment.ex, prompt_builder.ex, supervision_health.ex, affected_tests.ex, current_run_projections.ex, git.ex, tracker.ex, agent_chat.ex, asks_store.ex, boot.ex, agent_command_installer.ex, event_humanizer_helpers.ex, system_cpu.ex, provider_meter_snapshot.ex, webhooks.ex, external_content.ex, conversations.ex, process_identity.ex, decision_command_type.ex, distribution.ex, alert_topic.ex, current_run_outcome_snapshot.ex, shell.ex, opaque_identifier.ex). Cross-referenced by reading targeted slices outside the unit to verify claims: orchestrator/dispatcher.ex admission_probes, dispatch_policy.ex read_build_status/normalize_issue_state, capacity_binding.ex staleness, decision_store.ex executor notification paths, recent_merge_store.ex corruption handling, json_store.ex, log_file.ex, asks.ex, workflow_store.ex stamping, github/tracker.ex, linear/tracker.ex, agent_skills.ex shell_quote, aiur.ex start_distribution, and repo-wide greps for duplicated helpers (unsafe_control_chars?, truncate, shell escaping, kill -0, duration formatters, CLI envelopes, deterministic term hashing, AiurWeb references, Orchestrator facade callers). Tests: only scanned the unit's largest test files (agent_control_cli_test, build_gate_test, agent_environment_test, decision_attention_test, executor_events_test, supervision_health_test) with greps for known test-bug patterns plus a few targeted reads; did not read test files in full. Not verified: runtime behaviour (no builds/tests run); the OTP `deterministic` stability claim in loose-2-06 is from the OTP documentation, not an observed incident. Submodules behind the Orchestrator facade (PauseResume, StatusReport, Lifecycle, etc.) belong to other units and were only read where needed to confirm a claim.

findings.title: AgentControlCLI is a 3,408-line god module covering ~15 unrelated control surfaces
findings.description: One module owns status/agents/watch rendering, executor wake-stream claims/lease renewal, executor pub/sub, set max-agents, `--todo` GitHub label writes, reset-budget, global pause, operator message delivery confirmation, pause/resume confirmation polling, provider usage rendering, build-gate/supervision/CI/prewarm/listener status rendering, row visibility policy, the watch board with a persistent baseline, the RPC exit/error protocol, and a 160-line reason-to-text table. It aliases 37 modules across Orchestrator, Executor, GitHub, BuildGate, Asks, AlertFeed, ProviderMeterProjection and AiurWeb, so it will be pulled into every package the carve creates.
findings.evidence: wc -l = 3408. Responsibility ranges (approx): executor wake/claims 418-781 (~360 lines), todo 837-1164 (~330), pause/resume/message confirmation 1234-1874 (~640), status/capacity/build-gate/supervision rendering 1876-2631 (~750), watch board 2772-3025 (~250), reason table 3232-3402 (~170). Alias block lines 4-38 names 37 modules including `alias AiurWeb.OperatorControlCenter.UnitsPresentation`.
findings.recommendation: Split by surface into Aiur.CLI.Control.{Protocol (exit_marker/control_error/guarded/format_timeout_budget), Status, Agents, Watch, ExecutorWake, ExecutorClaims, Todo, PauseResume, Message, Usage, GlobalPause} and move reason rendering next to its producers (see loose-2-21). Keep AgentControlCLI as a thin RPC dispatch table only.
findings.refactor_hint: Belongs in a `aiur_cli` package that depends on public client APIs of orchestrator/executor/github packages; today it reaches into internals of each, so it must be split before those packages can be carved.

findings.title: `aiur status` serially aggregates ~10 blocking subsystem reads whose worst-case timeouts sum far past the 10s launcher budget
findings.description: After the (read-model backed, 5s-bounded) fleet view, print_status_report calls in sequence: ExecutorListener.bindings, ExecutorWakeInbox.stats (GenServer.call, default 5s), CodeOwners.trust_snapshot (GenServer.call, default 5s), Config.settings!, SupervisionHealth.status (GenServer.call 5s, which also re-evaluates the tree and may emit alerts), CiReadiness.cached_result, BuildGate.status (python3 + sh spawns with no timeout), RepoBase.status (5s), and Asks.open, which opens an EXCLUSIVE SQLite transaction with a 30s busy_timeout and replays the whole asks log. The code's own comments cite #1684, #1837 and #2329 as incidents of exactly this shape (a status command stalled behind one blocked dependency). Each fix moved one read off a mailbox; the aggregation pattern remained.
findings.evidence:
agent_control_cli.ex:214-218 `supervision_exit_code = print_supervision_health()
 print_ci_readiness()
 print_build_gate_status()
 print_prewarm_status()
 print_blocking_asks(opts)`; executor_wake_inbox.ex:98 `def stats(server \ __MODULE__), do: GenServer.call(server, :stats)`; code_owners.ex:105-106 `GenServer.call(server, :trust_snapshot)`; repo_base.ex:206 `GenServer.call(__MODULE__, :status, timeout)` (5_000); asks_store.ex:8 `@lock_timeout_ms 30_000` + line 20 `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE`; comment at agent_control_cli.ex:52-57 documents the 10s launcher kill.
findings.recommendation: Have each owning process publish its status section into the same SnapshotStore read model the fleet view uses (with observed_at), so `status` performs zero synchronous cross-process calls. Until then, run the section probes concurrently under one shared deadline (Task.async_stream with timeout) and render a timed-out section as `UNAVAILABLE (timed out)` rather than stalling the whole command.
findings.refactor_hint: The status read model (Orchestrator.SnapshotStore) should become a package-level 'observability' contract that subsystems write to; the CLI package then only reads it.

findings.title: BuildGate.status spawns unbounded external processes and writes /tmp files inside the Orchestrator dispatch admission path
findings.description: Dispatcher.admission_probes (run by maybe_choose_under_load inside the Orchestrator GenServer on each dispatch cycle) calls DispatchPolicy.read_build_status -> BuildGate.status. On Linux that writes a manifest to System.tmp_dir!, runs `python3 build_gate_holder.py --scan-locks-manifest` via System.cmd with no timeout, then spawns `sh -c 'kill -0 -PGID'` once per holder and one more python3 per `.hold-timeout` marker. A hung python (e.g. blocked lock/NFS) wedges the orchestrator mailbox indefinitely, the failure class behind #1837/#2137. The same scan also runs from BuildGateHoldMonitor (30s), RunTelemetry.Sampler and `aiur status`, so three independent pollers repeat it.
findings.evidence: build_gate.ex:243 `case System.cmd(python, [holder_path(), "--scan-locks-manifest", manifest_path], stderr_to_stdout: true) do` (no timeout); :251 `path = Path.join(System.tmp_dir!(), "aiur-build-gate-scan-...json")`; :664 `System.cmd(shell, ["-c", "kill -0 -#{pgid}"], ...)`; dispatcher.ex:948 `build_status: DispatchPolicy.read_build_status(),`; build_gate_hold_monitor.ex:30 `@default_interval_ms 30_000`; run_telemetry/sampler.ex:224 `&BuildGate.status/0`.
findings.recommendation: Make BuildGateHoldMonitor the single scanner: run the python scan through a Port with a hard timeout and kill-on-timeout (Aiur.Git.run_bounded_cmd already implements this), publish the result plus observed_at to ETS/persistent_term, and have admission, telemetry and the CLI read the cached snapshot with its age. Replace per-holder `sh kill -0` with a /proc check through ProcessIdentity. Pass the manifest over stdin instead of /tmp.
findings.refactor_hint: BuildGate is a host-resource package (build admission); its read API should be a cached snapshot so the orchestrator package never shells out on its own mailbox.

findings.title: ExecutorEvents treats an unreadable subscription file as empty, then overwrites it; all writers race without a lock
findings.description: subscription_state/0 maps every JsonStore.read error (corrupt JSON, EACCES, EMFILE) to `%{"subscribed_to" => [], "last_seen_event_id" => nil}` with no log or alert. The next subscribe/unsubscribe/advance_cursor/reconcile_subscriptions persists that empty state over the file, losing every manual subscription and resetting the cursor, so the next listen replays the whole journal. Separately, four writers do unlocked read-modify-write of the same file from different processes (CLI RPC subscribe/unsubscribe, the listen loop's advance_cursor per delivered event, ExecutorBindings.reconcile in the daemon), so concurrent writes lose updates (a cursor advance can erase a new subscription, or a reconcile can move the cursor backwards).
findings.evidence: executor_events.ex:455-464 `case JsonStore.read(subscription_path()) do {:ok, %{} = state} -> ... _ -> %{"subscribed_to" => [], "last_seen_event_id" => nil} end`; json_store.ex:45-51 returns `{:error, reason}` for undecodable content; advance_cursor 246-250 does `state = subscription_state() ... persist_subscription_state(%{state | "last_seen_event_id" => max(current, id)})` on every delivered event.
findings.recommendation: Return {:error, _} for anything but :enoent, refuse to persist over an unreadable file, and emit a needs_attention alert. Serialize all subscription/cursor mutations through one owner process (or a file lock like Asks.Store.with_lock) instead of per-caller RMW.
findings.refactor_hint: Executor event journal + cursor belongs in an executor-events package with a single writer process; the CLI should call it, not mutate its files.

findings.title: ExecutorEvents replays the entire, never-compacted journal on every dedup lookup, inside DecisionStore; one corrupt line latches all Command notifications
findings.description: publish_deferred/2, ensure_requested/1 and reconcile_requested/1 each call journal_events/0, which reads and decodes the whole append-only journal. Nothing compacts it (only IdGenerator also scans it). publish_deferred runs synchronously from DecisionStore.notify_lifecycle, so every deferral costs O(journal) file I/O on the DecisionStore process. If any line is corrupt, journal_events returns {:error, {:corrupt, ...}} and emits a needs_attention alert on every call; publish_deferred and ensure_requested then fail forever until an operator hand-repairs the file. DecisionStore's notify_deferred_executor only logs a warning on failure, with no retry (unlike requested notifications), so a deferred Command can silently never reach the Executor.
findings.evidence: executor_events.ex:416-429 `case DecisionLog.replay(journal_path(), &replay_validator/1) do ... {:ok, _events, {:corrupt, line, reason}} -> report_corruption(line, reason)`; decision_store.ex:2625-2628 `case ExecutorEvents.publish_deferred(decision) do ... {:error, reason} -> Logger.warning("aiur_decision_store phase=executor_notification_failed ...")`; grep finds no compaction of StatePaths.journal_path() (only readers: executor_events.ex:417, id_generator.ex:333, executor_wake_inbox.ex:103).
findings.recommendation: Maintain an in-memory index {topic, decision_id, version} -> event_id in the owning process (built once at boot) instead of replaying per call; add retention/compaction for the journal; skip-and-quarantine a corrupt line rather than failing all lookups; give deferred notifications the same retry schedule requested notifications have.
findings.refactor_hint: Same executor-events package as loose-2-04; DecisionStore should depend on its API through an async publish, not block on its file I/O.

findings.title: Persisted content hashes are computed from Erlang external term format of Elixir maps/structs, so an OTP upgrade or a new struct field invalidates every stored record
findings.description: RecentMerge.with_content_hash hashes `Map.from_struct(merge) |> :erlang.term_to_binary([:deterministic])`; DecisionValidation.content_hash does the same for Decision/Answer content. decode_record/from_json_safe recompute and compare to the persisted hash, and a mismatch is treated as corruption. OTP documents `deterministic` as stable only within one release, and Map.from_struct includes every struct field, so adding a field to RecentMerge (or any hashed map) changes every hash. The result is RecentMergeStore going permanently read-only at boot (apply_corruption sets writable?: false and alerts), and Decision answers/revisions/events failing to decode, with no automatic exit short of an operator deleting data.
findings.evidence: recent_merge.ex:320-326 `merge |> Map.from_struct() |> Map.delete(:content_hash) |> :erlang.term_to_binary([:deterministic]) |> then(&:crypto.hash(:sha256, &1))`; :309-313 `if with_content_hash(merge).content_hash == content_hash do {:ok, merge} else {:error, :content_hash_mismatch}`; decision_answer.ex:121 `compare_persisted(answer.content_hash, persisted_hash, :answer_content_hash_mismatch)`; recent_merge_store.ex:169 `%{state | writable?: false, health: {:corrupt, line, reason}}`. Other `[:deterministic]` hash sites: agent_queue_store.ex:491, progress_retention.ex:381, agent_runner/tool_executor.ex:725, app_server/tool_call_identity.ex:49, current_run_membership/event.ex:96, current_run_membership/store/checkpoint.ex:74, store/terminal_verification.ex:35, current_run_outcome_snapshot/membership_index.ex:39.
findings.recommendation: Introduce one Aiur.CanonicalHash that hashes a canonical JSON encoding (sorted keys, explicit field list taken from the to_record/to_json_safe shape, schema_version included). Migrate verifiers to accept the legacy hash once and rewrite. Never hash Map.from_struct of an evolving struct.
findings.refactor_hint: Put CanonicalHash in the shared persistence/core package that every store package depends on; do this before carving so stores in different packages agree on the format.

findings.title: Operator-actionable conditions are reported only through Logger, which writes nowhere unless AIUR_DEBUG is set
findings.description: LogFile.configure removes every logger handler when debug is off, so these sites drop their signal: Env boot notices (which integrations are disabled; that a ~/.aiur/.env value is being ignored because ./.env outranks it); DecisionAttention legacy import truncation beyond 100 attentions (the rest are never restored or re-asked), loader failures and per-attention rejections; BuildGate skipping unresolvable writable roots; CurrentRunProjections swallowing a failed PubSub subscription with no log at all (projections then refresh only on clock/reconcile ticks); Distribution monitor setup failure.
findings.evidence: log_file.ex:119-123 `# No --debug -> no aiur.log at all ... :ok = remove_existing_handler(); :ok = remove_default_console_handler()`; env.ex:232 `Enum.each(precedence_warnings(precedence_conflicts(home, repo)), &Logger.warning/1)`; decision_attention.ex:230-236 `{to_import, ignored} = Enum.split(attentions, state.import_limit) ... Logger.warning("decision_attention legacy_import_truncated ...")`; current_run_projections.ex:168-174 `defp safe_subscribe(fun) do fun.() rescue _error -> :ok catch _kind, _reason -> :ok end`.
findings.recommendation: Route every operator-actionable condition through Alerts (needs_attention) or a boot-notices section surfaced by `aiur status`; reserve Logger for debug detail. Add a lint rule (credo) flagging Logger.warning/error in a branch that also drops data. For DecisionAttention, page through all legacy attentions instead of truncating.
findings.refactor_hint: An 'operator notices' channel should be part of the core observability contract all carved packages emit into.

findings.title: SupervisionHealth commits the new `missing` set before alert delivery, so a failed degraded/resolved alert is never retried
findings.description: evaluate/1 computes `changed?`, stores `missing` into state, then calls notify/3, which rescues any delivery failure into a Logger.warning. The next check sees `missing == state.missing` and never re-emits, so a supervision degradation whose alert write failed stays invisible in the alert feed for as long as the degradation lasts.
findings.evidence: supervision_health.ex:113-117 `changed? = missing != state.missing ... state = state |> Map.put(:missing, missing) |> reconcile_monitors() ... if changed?, do: notify(state.alert_fun, snapshot, missing)`; :127-133 `defp notify(...) do alert_fun.(snapshot, missing) rescue exception -> log_alert_failure(exception)`.
findings.recommendation: Track `last_notified_missing` separately and update it only when notify succeeds; retry on the next tick otherwise.
findings.refactor_hint: Keep with the supervision/observability package; the fix is local.

findings.title: DecisionAttention re-asks forever every 15 minutes although its moduledoc promises bounded re-asks
findings.description: handle_info({:reask, key}) emits the alert and unconditionally reschedules; there is no attempt counter or cap. Each re-ask appends a needs_attention alert to the append-only alert feed (96 per day per open attention), and restored legacy attentions re-enter the same loop at boot.
findings.evidence: moduledoc line 7 `keeps an unanswered question visible with bounded re-asks`; :222-225 `emit(state.alert_emitter, attention); next_attention = schedule_reask(attention, state.reask_interval_ms)`; :17 `@default_reask_interval_ms :timer.minutes(15)`.
findings.recommendation: Add a re-ask budget (count or exponential backoff with a ceiling) stored on the attention, or fix the doc; dedupe re-asks in AlertFeed rather than appending new rows.
findings.refactor_hint: Decision/attention package; affects alert-feed growth shared with observability.

findings.title: DecisionAttention blocks its GenServer on a 60s DecisionStore write and raised its own call timeout to 65s to compensate
findings.description: handle_call({:open, ...}) calls project_attention -> DecisionStore.project_attention (a synchronous 60s call) inside the registry process, so every open, resolve and reask queues behind the slowest DecisionStore write. The comment documents the fix-by-raising-a-limit: the outer call timeout was raised to outlast the inner one.
findings.evidence: decision_attention.ex:19-21 `# The outer registry call must outlast DecisionStore's 60-second write call ... @open_timeout 65_000`; :153 `case project_attention(state.decision_projector, attention, opts) do` inside handle_call.
findings.recommendation: Project in the caller's process (or a Task with a deferred GenServer.reply) and call the registry only to register the already-projected result; then the registry call can use a short timeout.
findings.refactor_hint: Decision package; removes a cross-process timeout coupling between DecisionAttention and DecisionStore.

findings.title: `unsafe_control_chars?` is copied 9 times with two divergent policies
findings.description: Six copies allow \n/\t/\r and accept DEL (0x7F); decision_api.ex and config/schema/decisions.ex reject every byte < 0x20 including newlines and also reject DEL; decision_query/params.ex uses a regex `[\x00-\x1F\x7F]`. The same Decision text can be accepted by DecisionValidation and rejected at the API boundary (or vice versa). The surrounding bounded-text normalizers (optional_text/normalize_string/required_text) are duplicated in decision_answer.ex:223-255 and recent_merge.ex:374-387, 501-506 too.
findings.evidence: decision_validation.ex:202-205 `Enum.any?(fn codepoint -> codepoint < 0x20 and codepoint not in [?\n, ?\t, ?\r] end)` vs decision_api.ex:384-387 `Enum.any?(&(&1 < 0x20 or &1 == 0x7F))`.
findings.recommendation: Create Aiur.BoundedText with `normalize(value, max, field, allow_newlines?: bool)` and one control-character policy per field class; delete the private copies.
findings.refactor_hint: Shared validation helpers belong in the core package every Decision/merge package depends on.

findings.title: Shell quoting is re-implemented 4 more times despite Aiur.Shell claiming to be the only implementation; one copy is wrong
findings.description: Aiur.Shell's moduledoc says `This is the ONLY shell-escape implementation in the codebase`. AgentControlCLI and Claude.Repl.Command use the `'\''` dialect, mix aiur.affected_tests copies Shell's dialect verbatim, and agent_skills.ex replaces `'` with `'\"'\"'`, which leaves an unterminated quote for any value containing `'` (currently fed only internal skill paths, so latent). AgentEnvironment additionally hand-writes a shell `case` pattern that duplicates its own Elixir name lists.
findings.evidence: shell.ex:3-8 claims exclusivity; agent_control_cli.ex:1297 `defp shell_quote(text), do: "'" <> String.replace(text, "'", "'\\''") <> "'"`; agent_skills.ex:384 `defp shell_quote(value), do: "'" <> String.replace(value, "'", "'\\\"'\\\"'") <> "'"` used unquoted in `for skill_path in #{paths}; do` (357, 372).
findings.recommendation: Replace every private copy with Aiur.Shell.escape/1 and add a credo check banning `String.replace(_, "'", _)` outside shell.ex.
findings.refactor_hint: Aiur.Shell is a leaf utility for the core package; the copies sit in CLI, Claude, skills and mix-task packages that would otherwise each carry their own.

findings.title: Process liveness probes are duplicated with opposite failure semantics; BuildGate deletes slots when its probe fails
findings.description: ProcessIdentity.alive? returns true when the probe raises because `A probe failure is not evidence that a process is gone`. BuildGate.owner_alive?/process_group_alive? return false when `sh` is missing or System.cmd raises, and active_count then `File.rm_rf(slot_path)` on the pid strategy, reaping a possibly-live lease. All copies use `kill -0`, which also reports EPERM (process owned by another user) as dead. Five more ad-hoc `kill -0` shell-outs exist in Claude/opencode code.
findings.evidence: process_identity.ex:7-10 `rescue # A probe failure is not evidence that a process is gone ... _ -> true`; build_gate.ex:650-657 `case System.find_executable("sh") do nil -> false ... rescue _ -> false`; :578-584 `stale_owner_record?(slot_path) -> ... File.rm_rf(slot_path)`.
findings.recommendation: Give ProcessIdentity a tri-state `probe(pid | {:group, pgid}) :: :alive | :gone | :unknown` backed by /proc (falling back to `kill -0` that distinguishes ESRCH from EPERM) and make every destructive caller treat :unknown as alive.
findings.refactor_hint: ProcessIdentity is a core OS utility; BuildGate, Claude and opencode packages should depend on it instead of shelling out.

findings.title: Tracker state/label normalization is duplicated (twice inside AgentControlCLI alone) and has drifted; state slugs are hard-coded literals
findings.description: normalized_label/1 and normalized_tracker_state/1 in AgentControlCLI are identical trim+downcase functions. DispatchPolicy.normalize_issue_state trims and is nil-safe (a comment records that a missing clause crashed the orchestrator), while Config.Schema.AgentValidation.normalize_issue_state only downcases and raises on non-binaries. The literal "human-review" appears 20 times across 13+ files and "ci-wait" 8 times; the watch board hard-codes both.
findings.evidence: agent_validation.ex:11-13 `def normalize_issue_state(state_name) when is_binary(state_name) do String.downcase(state_name) end`; dispatch_policy.ex:1080-1081 `String.downcase(String.trim(state_name))`; agent_control_cli.ex:2779 `pr_ready? = state in ["human-review", "merging"]`.
findings.recommendation: Create Aiur.TrackerState with normalize/1 (nil-safe), label/2 (wrapping StatePolicy.state_label) and named slug constants; route CLI, orchestrator, config validation and turn loop through it.
findings.refactor_hint: A tiny shared 'tracker vocabulary' module in the core package; every carved package reads states through it.

findings.title: Duration/age formatting is reimplemented at least 13 times, 5 of them inside AgentControlCLI despite its own 'one age shape' comment
findings.description: AgentControlCLI's header says `One age shape wherever a stale surface appears — reuse #1814's renderer rather than adding a second one for the CLI`, yet the same module defines age_label ("5m ago"), format_gate_hold ("1h5m"), format_runtime ("1h5m" with different thresholds), cli_reset_suffix ("resets in 2d 3h") and poll_seconds. Each surface rounds and labels differently, so the same age reads differently across CLI, TUI and dashboard.
findings.evidence: agent_control_cli.ex:36-38 comment vs :2269-2272 `defp age_label(seconds) when seconds < 60, do: "#{seconds}s ago" ...` and :2762-2767 `seconds < 3600 -> "#{div(seconds, 60)}m"`; github_usage_cli.ex:251-252 `"#{div(seconds, 60)}m #{rem(seconds, 60)}s"`.
findings.recommendation: Add Aiur.Format.Duration (compact/1, ago/1, until/2) and have UnitsPresentation.age_label delegate to it; delete the private formatters.
findings.refactor_hint: Presentation-neutral formatting helpers belong in a shared 'presentation' package used by CLI, TUI and web.

findings.title: The versioned CLI JSON envelope (schema_version/page/snapshot/request/sources/data) is hand-rolled in 6 CLI modules and has drifted
findings.description: Each CLI rebuilds the envelope map, the `source` record (state/observed_at/age_ms/freshness/partial/reasons), age_ms/2 and unavailable_source/1. Drift: github-usage has no request/sources/auxiliary keys; build-orders is schema 2 and units/commands/analytics are 1; UnitsCLI.age_ms accepts nil while BuildOrdersCLI.age_ms requires two DateTimes; freshness mappings differ (:healthy->:current vs :fresh/:current->:current).
findings.evidence: build_orders_cli.ex:250 `defp unavailable_source(reason), do: %{state: :unavailable, observed_at: nil, age_ms: nil, freshness: :unknown, partial: true, reasons: [reason]}` is byte-identical to analytics_cli.ex:174; github_usage_cli.ex:73-78 envelope omits `request`/`sources`.
findings.recommendation: Extract Aiur.CLI.Envelope.new(page, schema_version, opts) and Aiur.CLI.Envelope.Source.{from_health, unavailable, unknown}; add a contract test that every `--json` command emits the required keys.
findings.refactor_hint: CLI package shared contract; also the natural home for the dashboard/CLI parity rule in AGENTS.md (observed_at/age_ms/freshness).

findings.title: Core CLI and projection modules depend on AiurWeb presenters and PubSub (reverse layering)
findings.description: Modules in the Aiur namespace import AiurWeb.OperatorControlCenter.{UnitsPresentation, PayloadLoader, UnitsPolicy, UnitsPresenter, BuildOrderGridModel}, AiurWeb.BuildOrder.{DataSource, Runtime}, AiurWeb.BuildOrderPresenter and AiurWeb.ObservabilityPubSub. The web layer cannot be carved out, and the CLI cannot ship without Phoenix, until these presenters and policies move to a UI-neutral package.
findings.evidence: agent_control_cli.ex:38 `alias AiurWeb.OperatorControlCenter.UnitsPresentation`; units_cli.ex:7 `alias AiurWeb.OperatorControlCenter.{PayloadLoader, UnitsPolicy, UnitsPresentation, UnitsPresenter}`; current_run_projections.ex:163 `&AiurWeb.ObservabilityPubSub.subscribe/0`.
findings.recommendation: Move the presenters/policies (they are pure data transforms) to an `Aiur.Presentation.*` namespace in a package both web and CLI depend on; give CurrentRunProjections an injected subscription list whose default lives in the web package.
findings.refactor_hint: Blocks the web/core split directly; do this first in the carve.

findings.title: AgentControlCLI uses 14 global Application-env function seams plus three other injection styles; its test suite needs 75 put_env calls and cannot run async
findings.description: Seams read on every call: agent_control_cli_busy_mailbox_threshold, _set_global_pause_fun, _message_fun, _message_status_fun, _message_confirm_timeout_ms, _global_pause_status_fun, _status_fun, _confirmation_status_fun, _resume_confirm_timeout_ms, executor_listener_alive_fun, _trust_snapshot_fun, supervision_health_status_fun, _pause_fun, _resume_fun. The same module also injects through keyword opts (:fleet_view, :global_pause_status, :blocking_asks, :delivery_modes), a deps map (todo_runtime_deps) and error_fun. Global mutable config for DI forces serial tests and lets one test's seam leak into another.
findings.evidence: grep: 14 `Application.get_env(:aiur, :..._fun...)` sites in agent_control_cli.ex; agent_control_cli_test.exs has 75 `Application.put_env` and 0 `async: true` (4052 lines). send_message 1356-1360 even dispatches on the seam's arity: `fun when is_function(fun, 3) -> ...; fun when is_function(fun, 2) -> ...`.
findings.recommendation: Define a `Deps` struct (or behaviour modules) passed through opts with production defaults, as todo/2 already does; remove the Application-env seams and the legacy arity-2 message seam.
findings.refactor_hint: Required for the CLI package to be testable in isolation from the daemon packages it calls.

findings.title: `aiur watch --changes` keeps one node-global baseline, so concurrent watchers (supported multi-Executor setups) consume each other's deltas
findings.description: The watch baseline is a single persistent_term key shared by every caller on the node. Multiple Executors are documented as `a supported configuration, not a fault`; when two consumers (or an Executor and a human) run `watch --changes`, whichever runs first advances the baseline and the other sees `(no changes)` for rows that did change. persistent_term.put also triggers a global scan of all processes on each update.
findings.evidence: agent_control_cli.ex:94 `@watch_baseline_key {__MODULE__, :watch_baseline}`; :2861-2863 `previous = :persistent_term.get(@watch_baseline_key, %{}) ... :persistent_term.put(@watch_baseline_key, current)`; :662-663 `multiple executors are a supported configuration, not a fault`.
findings.recommendation: Key the baseline by consumer id (Claims.resolve_consumer_id/1 already exists) in an ETS table owned by a long-lived process, or return an opaque cursor the caller passes back.
findings.refactor_hint: Watch state belongs with the executor package (per-consumer state), not the CLI module.

findings.title: Many control-RPC entrypoints bypass `guarded/2`, reintroducing the empty-output crash mode it was added to prevent
findings.description: guarded/2 exists because an unexpected raise/exit inside a command `used to kill the RPC evaluator outright, and the operator saw a non-zero exit with an empty buffer` (#1684). units/1, executor_emit/2, executor_subscribe/1, executor_unsubscribe/1, executor_subscriptions/0, executor_wait/1, executor_fast_forward/2, executor_roster/1, executor_claim/1, executor_release/1 and executor_revoke/2 are not wrapped, so any raise (e.g. Roster.build, JsonStore.write! inside a rescue-less path, Claims errors) produces no exit marker.
findings.evidence: agent_control_cli.ex:355-356 `def units(opts \\ []) do UnitsCLI.run(opts) |> exit_marker() end` vs :359-361 `def build_orders(...) do guarded("build-orders", fn -> ...`; comment at 3096-3101.
findings.recommendation: Dispatch every public command through a single `run(command, fun)` that applies guarded/2 and exit_marker/1, so a new command cannot forget it.
findings.refactor_hint: Part of the CLI Protocol module proposed in loose-2-01.

findings.title: Failure-reason rendering is a growing CLI-local table of special cases instead of living with the producers
findings.description: format_reason/1 has 36 clauses plus a 32-entry fallback map, many citing incidents; format_message_reason and print_failure add more. ExecutorCommandCLI.command_error has 20 clauses keyed on action strings. The dashboard and other surfaces that receive the same Orchestrator/DecisionStore errors cannot reuse this text. escalation_message/2 matches only :opened and :already_open, so any new status raises FunctionClauseError.
findings.evidence: agent_control_cli.ex:3232-3392 (~160 lines) e.g. `defp format_reason({:redispatch_deferred, :preferred_worker_unavailable}), do: "redispatch deferred because ..."`; executor_command_cli.ex:207-208 two-clause escalation_message with no fallback.
findings.recommendation: Have each producer expose `describe/1` for its error atoms (the StatusReason.render pattern already exists) and let every surface render through it; add a catch-all to escalation_message.
findings.refactor_hint: Error vocabularies move with their owning packages (orchestrator, decisions); the CLI package only formats.

findings.title: Status-row visibility is an incident-driven clause chain that exists only in the CLI
findings.description: visible_status_row?/2 is seven clauses of special cases (deactivated, latched #1712, claim_released #1475, orphaned/stale/workspace_ownership claims, idle-in-active-state, terminal) added one incident at a time. Only status and watch apply it; the dashboard and any other consumer of the same fleet view must reimplement or diverge.
findings.evidence: agent_control_cli.ex:2563-2571 `# A latched-out agent is idle but terminal ... (#1712). Keep the row visible even when the tracker-state filters below would hide it` and :2586-2589 `when reason in [:orphaned_claim, :stale_claim, :workspace_ownership_waiting]`.
findings.recommendation: Move the policy into Orchestrator.StatusReport (or the fleet view) as a `visible?` flag computed once per row, with a table-driven rule list; CLI and dashboard read the flag.
findings.refactor_hint: Belongs in the orchestrator read-model package, not the CLI.

findings.title: The CLI applies its own hard-coded 120s staleness rule for GitHub quota, contradicting the shared CapacityBinding rule it claims to use
findings.description: The comment says classification lives in CapacityBinding `so the CLI and the dashboards name the same constraint from the same rules`, but github_quota_measurement/1 decides staleness with a fixed `> 120` seconds and its own ISO-8601 parse, while CapacityBinding derives a poll-interval-relative window (2x interval clamped to 60-300s).
findings.evidence: agent_control_cli.ex:2098-2099 `defp stale_github_quota_measurement?(%DateTime{} = observed_at), do: DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(), observed_at, :second) > 120`; capacity_binding.ex:106-117 `@stale_sample_floor_ms 60_000 ... interval |> Kernel.*(2) |> max(@stale_sample_floor_ms) |> min(@stale_sample_ceiling_ms)`.
findings.recommendation: Add CapacityBinding.github_quota_freshness(hold, polling, now) and render from it.
findings.refactor_hint: Orchestrator capacity package owns the rule; CLI and dashboard only render.

findings.title: Orchestrator facade exposes ~100 delegates including dead entries, test-only shims and state-level functions its own submodules call back through
findings.description: Zero callers in lib or test: pause_issue_for_label_override/2, send_pause_control_message/2, resume_label_overridden_issue/2, log_tracker_fetch_error/1, log_tracker_preflight_error/1, github_next_poll_delay_ms/1, globally_paused?/0, read_cpu/1 (callers use TrackerHealth/PauseResume/DispatchPolicy directly). Test-only: six `*_for_test` functions and read_load, read_memory, prewarm_gate, load_gate, memory_gate, fd_gate, fd_headroom_threshold, load_envelope, overrunning_entry?, pane_interrupt_action(_no_pane), note_agent_activity_state. Meanwhile 12 submodules (reconciler 10 calls, comment_polling 9, issue_sync 7, comment_wake 7, push_routing 3, operator_messages 3, ...) call back into Aiur.Orchestrator for State-level operations (terminate_running_issue, running_worker_host, resume_paused_issue, ...), creating a facade<->submodule cycle.
findings.evidence: grep `Orchestrator.pause_issue_for_label_override(` etc.: 0 hits outside orchestrator.ex; orchestrator.ex:341-342 `def slot_status_for_test(%State{} = state), do: Slots.slot_status(state)`; `grep -rnE 'Orchestrator\.(terminate_running_issue|running_worker_host|resume_paused_issue|...)\(' lib` -> 49 calls from 12 orchestrator/* files.
findings.recommendation: Delete the dead delegates; point tests at the owning submodule; split the module into Aiur.Orchestrator.Client (process API) and the GenServer callbacks; make submodules call each other directly for State operations.
findings.refactor_hint: The orchestrator package's public surface should be the Client module only; the cycle must go before submodules can be moved independently.

findings.title: A pause/resume/message request crosses five pass-through layers; AgentChat adds only logging
findings.description: CLI -> AgentChat.pause/resume_with_receipt (one-line delegates) -> Aiur.Orchestrator.pause_agent (delegate) -> PauseResume.pause_agent (client) -> GenServer.call -> Orchestrator.handle_call -> PauseResume.pause_agent_call. Each layer re-declares the spec, and handle_call repeats an `{:error, :invalid_identifier}` fallback per message type.
findings.evidence: agent_chat.ex:106-108 `def pause(issue_identifier) when is_binary(issue_identifier) do Orchestrator.pause_agent(issue_identifier) end`; orchestrator.ex:457-460 `def pause_agent(identifier), do: PauseResume.pause_agent(identifier)`.
findings.recommendation: Collapse to one client module per concern (e.g. Aiur.Orchestrator.Control) that callers use directly; keep AgentChat only if it gains real behaviour (it could own the send-and-confirm loop currently in the CLI).
findings.refactor_hint: Defines the orchestrator package's public API; fewer layers means fewer modules to move.

findings.title: Aiur.Conversations is dead: zero references, and its moduledoc describes a call path that does not exist
findings.description: No module or test references Aiur.Conversations. The moduledoc says `The CLI's AgentList.App calls open/2 on Enter`, but AgentList.Activation calls PaneManager.open_conversation directly.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn Conversations lib test` -> only conversations.ex itself; activation.ex:96 `do: PaneManager.open_conversation(pane_manager, identifier, command, title: title)`.
findings.recommendation: Delete the module (or route AgentList through it if the attach/detach symmetry is still wanted).
findings.refactor_hint: Removes a TUI/pane-manager coupling from whatever package it would otherwise land in.

findings.title: Aiur.Distribution documents an epmd-loopback refusal it never performs and subscribes node events to a process that ignores them
findings.description: The moduledoc says `We refuse to enable distribution monitoring if that invariant is broken` and the result type includes `:epmd_not_local`, but start!/0 never checks ERL_EPMD_ADDRESS; epmd_address/0 and hidden_pane_nodes/0 are only used by tests. start!/0 calls :net_kernel.monitor_nodes from the application start process, which never handles nodeup/nodedown; PaneManager subscribes itself separately. The loopback invariant is actually enforced only by the launcher (aiur-engine.sh:366 `export ERL_EPMD_ADDRESS="127.0.0.1"`).
findings.evidence: distribution.ex:18 `@type result :: :ok | {:error, :not_distributed | :epmd_not_local}`; :46-48 `monitor_fn.(true, node_type: :hidden); :ok`; grep for epmd_not_local/epmd_address in lib -> only distribution.ex.
findings.recommendation: Either enforce the invariant (fail start when ERL_EPMD_ADDRESS is not loopback in distributed mode) or delete the module and the misleading security claim; drop the redundant monitor_nodes call.
findings.refactor_hint: Belongs in the launcher/boot package; security claims in docs should match code before the carve copies them.

findings.title: AgentEnvironment hand-maintains the same agent environment in three renderings that have already drifted
findings.description: workspace_env/2 (Port charlists, 110 lines), workspace_env_export_prefix/2 (SSH shell string, 67 lines) and scrub_shell_prefix/1 (shell unset list) each enumerate the variables separately. Drift: AIUR_CLAUDE_USAGE_TTL_MS is set only locally (remote agents get the adapter's default cadence); the remote path hard-codes `~/.aiur/github-budget` and `agent-token`, ignoring the :github_budget_dir override Budget.state_dir honours; AIUR_GITHUB_BUDGET_KEY is unset in the Port env and remote prefix but not in scrub_shell_prefix, which RepoBase, AppServer.Adapter, Codex.AppServerPort, Opencode.Server and Workspace.Hooks use; build-gate env is always exported locally but only with `build_gate: true` remotely; the shell case pattern at line 145 duplicates three Elixir name lists and patterns.
findings.evidence: agent_environment.ex:345 `{~c"AIUR_CLAUDE_USAGE_TTL_MS", String.to_charlist(usage_ttl_ms())}` has no counterpart in 436-467; :446 `"export AIUR_GITHUB_BUDGET_ROOT='~/.aiur/github-budget'\n"`; :267 `["AIUR_GITHUB_BUDGET_KEY"]` and :450 `"unset AIUR_GITHUB_BUDGET_KEY\n"` vs scrub_shell_prefix 130-141 (absent).
findings.recommendation: Define one declarative list of `%{name, value: fun(ctx), scope: :local | :remote | :both, scrub?: bool}` and render Port env, shell exports and unset lists from it; add a parity test asserting every exported name appears in each rendering or is explicitly scoped.
findings.refactor_hint: Agent-sandbox/environment package; the parity matters for the security invariants (#2266, #2356) documented in this file.

findings.title: Credential and provider env-var name lists are duplicated outside Env.Schema (including the bash launcher)
findings.description: Env.Schema already tags variables with groups (:github_app, :provider_keys), yet env.ex hard-codes the GitHub credential group and provider key names, AgentEnvironment keeps its own provider/App/GitHub token lists, and the launcher keeps GITHUB_CREDENTIAL_ENV_NAMES. Adding a provider key to the schema does not scrub it from agents (only the `*_API_KEY` pattern saves the common case) or count it in the disabled-integrations notice.
findings.evidence: env.ex:402 `names = ["DEEPSEEK_API_KEY", "MOONSHOT_API_KEY", "OPENROUTER_API_KEY", "OPENROUTER_MANAGEMENT_KEY"]`; agent_environment.ex:31 `@provider_credential_env_names ~w(DEEPSEEK_API_KEY MOONSHOT_API_KEY OPENROUTER_API_KEY OPENROUTER_MANAGEMENT_KEY)`; aiur-engine.sh:604 `GITHUB_CREDENTIAL_ENV_NAMES="GITHUB_TOKEN GITHUB_APP_ID ..."`.
findings.recommendation: Expose Schema.names_in_group/1 and derive all Elixir lists from it; generate the launcher constant (or test that it equals the schema group).
findings.refactor_hint: Env.Schema should be the single source in the config package; the launcher repo (if split) needs a generated or tested copy.

findings.title: PromptBuilder mojibakes the whole prompt when any byte is invalid; four divergent UTF-8 repair strategies exist
findings.description: ensure_utf8/1 reinterprets the entire rendered prompt as latin1 if it is not valid UTF-8, which double-encodes every valid multibyte character (em dashes and arrows in the shared instructions and operator template) instead of repairing the bad bytes. AgentEventFeed drops invalid bytes, Events.Sanitizer re-encodes as latin1 then falls back to replace_invalid, and TicketDetailSanitizer uses String.replace_invalid.
findings.evidence: prompt_builder.ex:186-191 `if String.valid?(binary) do binary else # Replace invalid bytes so Jason.encode! won't crash\n :unicode.characters_to_binary(binary, :latin1, :utf8)`; agent_event_feed.ex:264-265 drops bytes; ticket_detail_sanitizer.ex:185 `|> String.replace_invalid()`.
findings.recommendation: Add Aiur.Text.scrub_utf8/1 = String.replace_invalid/2 (replacement char) and use it in all four places.
findings.refactor_hint: Shared text utility in core; affects agent prompt fidelity.

findings.title: The Tracker behaviour mixes issue-tracker and code-host (PR) concerns; its conditional fallback is duplicated and the CLI bypasses it
findings.description: Tracker callbacks include fetch_open_pull_request(s)_for_branch, fetch_classified_pr_review_comments and fetch_unaddressed_pr_review_thread_comments; Linear and memory adapters stub them to `{:ok, nil}`/`{:ok, []}`, so a Linear-tracked repo hosted on GitHub silently never sees its PRs. The `function_exported?(..., :fetch_issue_states_by_ids_conditional, 2)` fallback is implemented both in Aiur.Tracker and again in Aiur.GitHub.Tracker. AgentControlCLI.todo calls Aiur.GitHub.Tracker directly and refuses non-GitHub trackers rather than going through the behaviour.
findings.evidence: linear/tracker.ex:98 `def fetch_open_pull_request_for_branch(_issue_id), do: {:ok, nil}`; tracker.ex:59-63 and github/tracker.ex:119-123 contain the same `if Code.ensure_loaded?(...) and function_exported?(...) ... else with {:ok, issues} <- ...fetch_issue_states_by_ids(issue_ids), do: {:ok, issues, cache}`; agent_control_cli.ex:1101 `fetch_issue: fn issue_id -> GitHubTracker.fetch_issue_states_by_ids([issue_id]) end`.
findings.recommendation: Split into Aiur.Tracker (issues, labels, states, comments) and Aiur.CodeHost (branches, PRs, reviews); keep the conditional fallback in one layer; make `--todo` use Tracker.add_label/remove_label.
findings.refactor_hint: Directly shapes the tracker vs GitHub-code-host package boundary in the carve.

findings.title: Aiur.CLI turns launch flags into VM-global Application env and computes the git revision at compile time
findings.description: Nine flags are written with Application.put_env (log_file, server_port_override, server_host_override, interactive_cli, headless, executor_mode, no_dashboard, launch_globally_paused, max_concurrent_agents_override) and read back from arbitrary modules, an implicit global config channel. `@git_rev` shells out to `git rev-parse` during compilation, so builds from a tarball or a dirty tree embed an empty or misleading revision. The moduledoc still says `Escript entrypoint` although the release runs it via eval with AIUR_ARGV_FILE.
findings.evidence: cli.ex:11-16 `@git_rev String.trim(case System.cmd("git", ["rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"], ...)`; :545 `Application.put_env(:aiur, :executor_mode, true)`; :564 `Application.put_env(:aiur, :launch_globally_paused, true)`.
findings.recommendation: Parse flags into a %LaunchOptions{} struct stored once (persistent_term or passed to the supervisor child specs) and read through one accessor; stamp the revision from the build script (it already sets AIUR_BUILD_STAMP).
findings.refactor_hint: Launcher/boot package; the carve needs an explicit launch-options contract between the CLI and the daemon packages.

findings.title: 19 `truncate` helpers with different byte/grapheme semantics; EventHumanizerHelpers.truncate appends '...' to strings it did not shorten
findings.description: EventHumanizerHelpers.truncate guards on byte_size(value) > max but slices by graphemes, so a 40-character string of 3-byte characters (120 bytes) with max 80 is returned whole with '...' appended. Other copies use '…', count graphemes, or cut bytes; grep finds 19 definitions across lib.
findings.evidence: event_humanizer_helpers.ex:34-35 `def truncate(value, max) when byte_size(value) > max do value |> String.slice(0, max) |> Kernel.<>("...")`; agent_control_cli.ex:2755-2756 uses String.length and '…'.
findings.recommendation: One Aiur.Text.truncate(value, max, unit: :grapheme | :byte, ellipsis: "…") used everywhere; fix the byte/grapheme mismatch.
findings.refactor_hint: Shared text utility in core.

findings.title: BuildGate read paths mutate state, report the wrong directory, and parse the same lease record four ways
findings.description: status/1 on the pid strategy deletes stale slots (a query with a destructive side effect). reduce_scan_result/1, scan_detail/1 and scan_issue/1 fallbacks report `gate_dir()` (the global default) instead of the gate_dir being scanned, so an override path is misreported. Lease metadata is parsed by parse_v2_record/1, owner_pid/1 (assumes pid= is the first line), owner_pgid/1 (searches any line) and int_field/2. hook_path/0 and holder_path/0 duplicate the priv path join; `python3` is looked up in two places.
findings.evidence: build_gate.ex:286 `do: {0, 0, [], [status_issue(:lock_probe_failed, gate_dir(), :invalid_scan_result)]}`; :628 `["pid=" <> value | _] <- String.split(record, "\n", trim: true)` vs :638 `Enum.find(..., &String.starts_with?(&1, "pgid="))`.
findings.recommendation: Parse a lease record once into a struct via parse_v2_record; thread gate_dir through the scan reducers; move stale-slot reaping to the monitor process.
findings.refactor_hint: Local cleanup inside the build-admission package.

findings.title: RecentMerge smuggles closing references into the 500-char display summary so reconciliation can re-parse them, silently dropping references that do not fit
findings.description: Because the struct is hashed (loose-2-06), closing references are not persisted as a field; normalized_summary appends `\nCloses #N` lines to the truncated, redacted summary and closing_issue_identifiers re-parses that display text. closing_reference_suffix skips any reference that would push the summary past 500 chars, so a PR closing roughly 38+ tickets leaves some tickets open with no signal.
findings.evidence: recent_merge.ex:115-116 `This remains derived rather than persisted so existing merge-audit records retain their original content hashes.`; :414-418 `if String.length(candidate) <= @summary_max, do: candidate, else: suffix`.
findings.recommendation: After the canonical-hash migration, persist `closing_issue_identifiers` as its own field and keep `summary` display-only.
findings.refactor_hint: Merge-audit store in the GitHub/outcomes package.

findings.title: Asks reads take an EXCLUSIVE SQLite lock with a 30s busy timeout and replay the whole log; file name does not match module
findings.description: Asks.open/1 -> all/1 wraps a read in Store.with_lock (BEGIN EXCLUSIVE, busy_timeout 30_000), so every `aiur status` and `aiur watch` can block up to 30s behind a writer and always decodes the full append-only log. The after-block issues COMMIT even when BEGIN failed. The file asks_store.ex defines Aiur.Asks.Store, which breaks the path-mirrors-module convention used elsewhere.
findings.evidence: asks.ex:57 `def all(repo) when is_binary(repo), do: Store.with_lock(repo, fn -> all_unlocked(repo) end)`; asks_store.ex:20 `sqlite_exec(connection, "BEGIN EXCLUSIVE", path)`; :24 `_ = Basic.exec(connection, "COMMIT")`.
findings.recommendation: Serve reads without the exclusive lock (the append protocol already tolerates a torn tail) or from an in-memory projection; move the file to asks/store.ex.
findings.refactor_hint: Asks store package.

findings.title: Workflow resolves sibling-file keys in two parallel code paths and keeps the config path in both the process dictionary and global app env
findings.description: resolve_hooks/resolve_prewarm/resolve_alerts/resolve_prompt (parse path) and resolved_prompt_file_path/resolved_hooks_file_path/resolved_prewarm_file_path (WorkflowStore stamping) each implement `Path.expand(rel, Path.dirname(path))` per key, and the latter three each re-read and re-parse the YAML (WorkflowStore now memoizes by digest to hide the cost, workflow_store.ex:390-399). The active path lives in Process dictionary + Application env purely for test isolation (#2287).
findings.evidence: workflow.ex:386-389 and 403-406 are the same `with {:ok, content} <- File.read(config_path), {:ok, config} <- yaml_to_map(content), rel when is_binary(rel) and rel != "" <- Map.get(config, KEY)` differing only by key.
findings.recommendation: Parse once into a struct that carries resolved sibling paths (prompt, hooks, prewarm, alerts) and have WorkflowStore read them from it; inject the config path explicitly in tests instead of the process-dictionary override.
findings.refactor_hint: Config package.

findings.title: Orchestrator info handlers destructure a handle_call reply tuple from Lifecycle.request_refresh
findings.description: handle_info(:github_quota_recovered) and handle_info({:github_budget_pause_expired, ...}) call Lifecycle.request_refresh/1, which returns `{:reply, result, state}`, and pattern-match it with `=`. Any change to the reply shape crashes the orchestrator from an info handler.
findings.evidence: orchestrator.ex:218 `{:reply, _result, state} = Lifecycle.request_refresh(state)`; :229 same.
findings.recommendation: Split Lifecycle.request_refresh into a state-transform returning {state, result} and wrap it into a reply only in handle_call.
findings.refactor_hint: Orchestrator lifecycle submodule.

findings.title: ProviderMeterSnapshot repeats its default health map three times
findings.description: The struct default, unknown/2 and health/1 each spell out the same six-key health map; unknown/2 could call health(:unknown_account_generation).
findings.evidence: provider_meter_snapshot.ex:83-90 inline map identical to health/1 at 94-103 except the failure atom.
findings.recommendation: Use health/1 in unknown/2 and the struct default (via a module attribute).
findings.refactor_hint: Provider meters package; trivial.

findings.title: Tests for this unit are serial, global-state-driven and sleep-timed
findings.description: agent_control_cli_test.exs (4,052 lines) has 75 Application.put_env calls and no async; ordering depends on Process.sleep (e.g. sleeping 30ms before enqueueing a wake against a 300ms executor_wait timeout, which can race on a loaded CI runner). build_gate_test.exs (3,231 lines) uses real bash/python holders with wall-clock sleeps of 1.5s and 2s to assert idle windows. Neither file runs async, so both add directly to suite wall time.
findings.evidence: agent_control_cli_test.exs:75-79 `capture_io(fn -> AgentControlCLI.executor_wait(timeout_ms: 300, json: true, as: "late-wake") end) ... Process.sleep(30) :ok = ExecutorWakeInbox.enqueue(...)`; build_gate_test.exs:1267 `Process.sleep(1_500)`, :1303 `Process.sleep(2_000)`.
findings.recommendation: After the Deps refactor (loose-2-18), make CLI tests async with injected deps; synchronize on explicit signals (e.g. a claim-acquired message) instead of sleeps; keep a small tagged set of real-process build-gate tests and unit-test the rest against a fake scanner.
findings.refactor_hint: Test suites move with their packages; global env seams would otherwise leak across package test runs.
